note: make rebaseline can leave the tree WORSE than it found it under memory pressure, and the damage lands BEFORE the error message. OBSERVED (The Quadrat, Mac, 2026-08-27): the tropes-report job died with Killed: 9 (OOM) partway through its output redirect, truncating the COMMITTED artifact docs/audits/trope-coverage-tvtropes-2012.md to EMPTY; the script reported its non-zero exit afterwards, so the message arrived after the file was already destroyed. Recovered with git checkout -- on that path, and the re-run was clean. THE GENERAL SHAPE, which is the part worth keeping: every artifact regenerate-artifacts.sh writes by output redirect (the render and report jobs, e.g. around lines 507-510 and 862-880) is truncated at open() time, not at write time — so ANY death mid-job, whether OOM, a kill or a timeout, empties the target first and explains itself second. TWO CONSEQUENCES. First, a rebaseline that dies is not a no-op you can simply retry from: run git status before retrying. Second, if a truncated artifact were committed, the drift check over docs/generated-paths.txt would read CLEAN on the empty file, because it compares the tree to the index rather than to what the generator should produce. OUR MEMORY PRESSURE WAS SELF-INFLICTED: back-to-back 800-second test binaries in the same session on the same box. If you are running long suites and a rebaseline together, space them.
